item.title: Ashutosh Bhadouria
item.description: Personal website of Ashutosh (Ashu) Bhadouria, a chemical engineer with a PhD from Purdue University working on electrochemistry and catalysis, and an incoming postdoctoral scholar at Caltech.

item.title: me, myself and I
item.description: CV of Ashutosh Bhadouria: education (Purdue University, UC Berkeley), research and work experience, awards, and contact links (Google Scholar, LinkedIn, email).

item.title: research
item.description: Research of Ashutosh Bhadouria on electrochemistry and catalysis, including electrochemical propane activation on Pt electrodes, plus class notes on chemical engineering, DFT and electrochemical engineering.

item.title: Chem 104A Midterm 1 Review
item.description: Chem 104A (inorganic chemistry) review notes — Bohr model and quantum numbers, orbitals and nodes, Slater's rules, VSEPR, Bent's rule and point groups, term symbols, acid–base theory (Brønsted, superacids, inductive/steric effects, Lewis acids, HSAB, Drago–Wayland), group theory and character tables, MO and VB theory, and main-group (hydrogen, boron, boranes, carboranes) chemistry.

item.title: Organic Chemistry pKa Cheat Sheet
item.description: Organic chemistry cheat sheet — Henderson–Hasselbalch and a pKa table (mineral acids, oxyacids, nitrogen acids, carbonyl α-hydrogens, bases), inductive effects and acyl reactivity, NMR shift positions, reactions of carbonyls (Grignard, carboxylation, oxidation, amide, ester, acid and imine formation, Wittig, acid chlorides), and the 20 amino acids by side-chain class.

item.title: Chemistry
item.description: General, inorganic and organic chemistry: atomic structure, bonding, periodic trends, and acids and bases.

item.title: HW 1
item.description: Revised HW 1 — the same Heun and Adams–Moulton results, plus the full Newton–Raphson Jacobian for the non-linear flat-plate conduction problem, the boundary-condition derivatives, the Thomas-algorithm update loop and the grid-independence plots.

item.title: HW 1
item.description: HW 1 — Heun's method (2nd-order Runge–Kutta) for a second-order ODE, the implicit 2nd-order Adams–Moulton (trapezoidal) method solved with Newton–Raphson, and steady conduction in a flat plate with variable conductivity and heat generation set up as a tridiagonal system.

item.title: HW 2
item.description: HW 2 — classifying PDEs by order and linearity, the inviscid Burgers equation in non-conservative and conservative upwind form with exact characteristic solutions, weak solutions, shock speed and the entropy condition, and classifying second-order PDEs by eigenvalues and canonical form.
